newsitem.title: UK: London gold, silver edge higher on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: London gold, silver edge higher on short-covering.

text.p: Gold and silver crept slightly higher on Tuesday as the market focused on expectations of a U.S. interest rate rise later in the day, dealers said.
Gold bullion closed at $382.05 an ounce, up $0.80 from Monday's London close, after ending lower for four days running.
Dealers said it had found a comfortable groove in the centre of its two-week-old $380-$385 range since losing ground last week from the backlash of a big a sell-off in silver.
"Gold has found support at $381-$382. But I don't think it's out of the mire yet," a dealer said.
The market was looking for direction from the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting, which dealers expected to raise short-term interest rates by one quarter percentage point.
But opinions were mixed as to whether or not an interest rate rise, which would increase the holding costs of gold, would have much of an effect on the market.
"The expectations are for a modest rise. I think it's been built into the prices so we're not exactly waiting with bated breath," one dealer said.
Stock and currency markets were holding their breath until after the FOMC's decision, which would not be known until after European trading was over.
Precious metals prices headed south late last week when U.S. investment funds launched a speculative play. Silver was the worst hit, plummeting below the key $5.00 an ounce level.
Silver finished off the day's highs at $4.89 an ounce, just one cent up from Monday's closing level.
Dealers and analysts said prices were likely to move sideways for at time, or even edge higher, before shifting lower again if the funds had another go at the downside.
In technical terms, gold held the key to the fate of the complex since last week's big sell-off of silver, analysts said.
"It's really a matter of which will be stronger -- will silver scramble up again in the absence of gold's backing, or will gold follow silver down as well?" an analyst said.
Platinum bounced to a high of $388.00 an ounce, after fixing at a fresh 2-1/2 year low on Monday. But it eased from the highs and finished just $0.10 firmer than on Monday, at $386.60.
Palladium, which sank to three-year lows this week, remained vulnerable and closed down $0.25 at $117.50 an ounce.
